prs.title: fix(server): allow JSON Accept in JSON response mode
prs.author: Genmin
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Streamable HTTP JSON response mode rejects requests with a 406 error unless the Accept header lists both `application/json` and `text/event-stream`. When the server is configured for JSON-only response mode, a client sending only `Accept: application/json` should be accepted, but the existing check in webStandardStreamableHttp.ts requires both media types unconditionally. Both PRs edit the same Accept-header validation branch (~line 598-614) to fix this, and their changeset descriptions describe the identical fix. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Streamable HTTP JSON response mode rejects requests with a 406 error unless the Accept header lists both `application/json` and `text/event-stream`. When the server is configured for JSON-only response mode, a client sending only `Accept: application/json` should be accepted, but the existing check in webStandardStreamableHttp.ts requires both media types unconditionally. Both PRs edit the same Accept-header validation branch (~line 598-614) to fix this, and their changeset descriptions describe the identical fix. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #1996 replaces the check with a dedicated `acceptsMediaType()` parser that correctly handles Accept-header syntax: it splits on `;` to strip parameters, treats a `q=0` parameter as explicitly not-accepted, and compares type/subtype pairs (with wildcard support), matching RFC 7231 semantics for content negotiation. #2046 instead does a direct substring `.includes('application/json')` check on the raw header, which doesn't account for quality values (e.g. `application/json;q=0` would still match as accepted) or structured type/subtype comparison, making it more prone to accepting malformed or explicitly-rejected Accept headers. #1996's logic is also factored into a standalone helper function, which is easier to unit test independently of the request handler.

clusters.pick_reason: #1996 replaces the check with a dedicated `acceptsMediaType()` parser that correctly handles Accept-header syntax: it splits on `;` to strip parameters, treats a `q=0` parameter as explicitly not-accepted, and compares type/subtype pairs (with wildcard support), matching RFC 7231 semantics for content negotiation. #2046 instead does a direct substring `.includes('application/json')` check on the raw header, which doesn't account for quality values (e.g. `application/json;q=0` would still match as accepted) or structured type/subtype comparison, making it more prone to accepting malformed or explicitly-rejected Accept headers. #1996's logic is also factored into a standalone helper function, which is easier to unit test independently of the request handler.
